meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-23
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood, AE); Devon Park (Redwood, SE); Liam Ortega (Redwood, CSM); Lena Ortiz (Sapphire, Head of Procurement); Mark Waters (Sapphire, CISO); Samir Patel (Sapphire, VP Eng); Ruth Delgado (Sapphire Legal)
summary: Procurement-focused call to review MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, pricing tiers, and onboarding steps for a pilot. Customer emphasized data residency and audit trail requirements; legal asked about indemnity and breach notification timelines. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options, KMS/HSM key management, and proposed commitment tiers for Dedicated capacity. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlined documents, security package, and priced pilot proposal; schedule legal-only session next week.
topics: Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off, we have Devon our solutions eng and Liam on success, uh quick roll call?
[00:07] Lena Ortiz: hi lena here from procurement, we've got mark waters from security and samir on the line, and ruth from legal joining now
[00:15] Mark Waters: hey everyone, yes on mute usually, but i'll chime in on the security bits

[00:21] Devon Park: awesome, thanks, goal for today is to walk through the MSA/DPA open items, SLA asks, and the pricing tiers we sent - make sure procurement and legal have what you need to move to approvals
[00:33] Ruth Delgado: yes we're mainly focused on indemnity caps, data breach notification windows, and DPA scoping for PII - also residency - we run in multiple regions so need clarity
[00:45] Maya Chen: understood, on indemnity the standard redwood language is in the MSA but we're open to discuss narrow carve-outs, can you flag the clauses you want redlined?
[00:53] Ruth Delgado: we'll send a markup, main ask is to reduce the cap for third-party claims and tighten notification to 48 hours not 72 - is that feasible?

[01:02] Devon Park: technically notification is straightforward, we do have our incident response SLA that aligns to 48 hours for first notification in most enterprise contracts, we can propose that in the MSA redline

[01:18] Samir Patel: thanks, from an engineering side we also need throughput guarantees for the pilot - 200 qps with p95 latency under 250ms for generation calls, what's realistic on your Dedicated offering?

[01:30] Devon Park: good question - Dedicated with reserved GPU pools targets those SLAs; for 200 qps depends on model and seq length, but for typical 2k token gen on a 8xA100-ish pool we can get p95 < 250ms with the right batching settings, i'll follow up with a capacity calc
[01:46] Mark Waters: and on data residency - do you offer a private deployment inside our VPC? we need logs to stay in our region and keys managed by our KMS or HSM
[01:56] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem installs, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for envelope encryption; devon will share the KMS integration doc and network diagram
[02:10] Mark Waters: perfect, also need to know retention windows for audit logs and what exposures are in the hosted offering if we choose that route

[02:18] Devon Park: hosted keeps metadata and logs per our retention defaults but we can offer extended retention as an add-on; for Private the logs are customer-controlled, and we provide audit log schema and sampling, we'll include examples in the security pack
[02:31] Ruth Delgado: on breach notification, liability aside, are there any third-party subprocessors listed? our DPA requires a subprocessors list and flow-down obligations
[02:38] Maya Chen: yes we have a subprocessors schedule, typically cloud infra and monitoring vendors - we'll attach the current list to the redline package
[02:46] Lena Ortiz: on pricing approvals: procurement needs visibility on tiered discounts if we commit to 12 months vs month-to-month; also need a pilot price for the first 3 months

[02:56] Maya Chen: the pricing spreadsheet has committed capacity tiers - 12-month commitments get a 15% discount on base unit price, 36-month better; pilot can be a time-limited discounted block, i'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet we send
[03:08] Samir Patel: will the pilot allow us to run perf benches? we want to run our synthetic workload and compare latency/cost numbers to our internal baseline

[03:16] Devon Park: absolutely - we can support a benchmark window, and we provide guidance on running our stress harness; note that KV cache and prefix caching behaviors can change per model, and that affects token cost - slight mis-trans in docs sometimes calls it K V cash but it's K V cache - we'll include recommended prompt strategies
[03:34] Mark Waters: ok i'd like to see the SOC 2 type II report and the most recent pen test; are those included in the security pack?
[03:41] Devon Park: yes SOC2 and ISO27001 cert are in the pack, plus summary of pen test results and remediation notes, and our AWS/GCP infra diagrams, we'll redact customer-specific info of course
[03:52] Ruth Delgado: on breach notification, do you accept contractual language for 48 hour notice and cooperation obligations? also encryption at rest and in transit needs to be specified

[04:02] Maya Chen: yes encryption at rest and in transit are standard, we support customer-managed keys for Private, and for hosted we can offer bring-your-own-key for enterprise customers via KMS integrations, we'll propose concrete language in the DPA
[04:14] Lena Ortiz: procurement timeline - if we get redlines by Monday and legal reviews within the week, can we expect a signed MSA by mid-August?
[04:22] Maya Chen: that's realistic, assuming no major commercial changes - pilot can start as soon as the SOW and payment terms are agreed, usually a 2- to 4-week ramp
[04:30] Samir Patel: one technical question: how do you handle model version pinning and rollouts? we need deterministic outputs for customer-facing features during pilot

[04:38] Devon Park: we support model pinning per route, and rollouts via canary/A-B with automatic fallback policies; logging of model version and prompts is part of auditability, we'll show console screenshots
[04:50] Mark Waters: what about e-discovery and data-subject requests? our legal needs a process flow
[04:57] Liam Ortega: we have documented DSR and e-discovery workflows, including how to extract logs and redact PII; we'll include a short playbook in the security pack
[05:06] Lena Ortiz: are there any hard stops we should know about from your side? like minimum commitments or lead times for dedicated capacity?
[05:14] Maya Chen: Dedicated usually needs a 4-6 week lead for GPU provisioning depending on region, and minimum reserved commit options are listed in the pricing - we'll highlight those in the sheet
[05:25] Ruth Delgado: one more on insurance and indemnity - can you send your certificate of insurance and confirm cyber liability limits?
[05:32] Maya Chen: yes COI and cyber liability summary included in the security pack
[05:39] Samir Patel: regarding feature flags and routing - can we route lower-priority traffic to cheaper model variants during peak to preserve SLOs?

[05:47] Devon Park: yes, smart routing policies allow routing by cost/latency/region and automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants, that is part of Redwood Optimize recommendations, though transcription in some earlier docs says "redwood optimizee" - we'll clarify
[05:59] Mark Waters: thanks, that helps from a cost-control perspective, procurement will want explicit terms on overage billing and notification thresholds
[06:07] Lena Ortiz: agreed, please put billing thresholds and grace periods in the SOW
[06:13] Maya Chen: will do, we'll add a billing thresholds section and example invoices to the package
[06:20] Ruth Delgado: ok next steps summarized?

[06:24] Maya Chen: recap: 1) send redlined MSA/DPA + pricing by 2026-07-27, 2) Devon sends security pack (SOC2, ISO, pen test, KMS integration, audit log samples) by 2026-07-25, 3) Samir sends throughput and SLA targets for pilot by 2026-07-26, 4) schedule legal-only review 2026-07-30 - any additions?
[06:41] Lena Ortiz: that's correct, please cc procurement on the redline thread
[06:45] Maya Chen: absolutely, i'll cc procurement and legal, thanks everyone for your time
[06:50] Mark Waters: thanks, bye
[06:52] Samir Patel: thanks all, bye
[06:54] Call ended
